name: Marriott International
description: Marriott International is the world's largest hotel company by room count, operating an asset-light franchise and management model across roughly 30 brands spanning luxury to select-service. It does not own the vast majority of its hotels; instead, independent owners and real estate investors finance and own the buildings, and Marriott collects franchise fees (a percentage of room revenue) and management fees (a base percentage of total revenue plus an incentive fee tied to profitability) in exchange for the brand, reservations system, loyalty program (Marriott Bonvoy) and, where applicable, day-to-day operations. This structure produces very high margins on fee revenue and minimal capital intensity relative to owning real estate. Growth is driven primarily by expanding the pipeline of hotels under development and by RevPAR (revenue per available room) gains across the existing system, supplemented by scale-driven ancillary revenue such as co-branded credit card fees.

businessLines.name: U.S. & Canada
businessLines.description: Marriott's largest and most mature segment, covering franchise and management fees earned from the roughly two-thirds of its systemwide rooms located in the U.S. and Canada.

businessLines.name: Europe, Middle East & Africa (EMEA)
businessLines.description: Franchise and management fees from Marriott's EMEA hotel system, a fast-growing international region for the company.

businessLines.name: Greater China
businessLines.description: Franchise and management fees from Marriott's Greater China hotel system.

businessLines.name: Asia Pacific excluding China (APEC)
businessLines.description: Franchise and management fees from Marriott's Asia-Pacific hotel system outside Greater China.
